correctness.rationale: For the zero-field Gibbs weight with exponent S_N^2/(2N), the Hubbard–Stratonovich identity makes the block exactly a latent-field product mixture. With X_N=N^(1/4)H_N the exponent is N F(N^(-1/4)x), F(h)=h^2/2-log cosh(h), with quartic leading term x^4/12. The global bound c min(x^4,sqrt(N)x^2) dominates exp(A x^2) times the rescaled density for each fixed A and large enough N, splitting at |x|=N^(1/4). Hence the block likelihood converges locally uniformly in the normalized spin sum, and the reference-law CLT gives weak convergence of those likelihoods. Independent replicas give the exact second-moment factor (1+tanh(H_N)tanh(H_N'))^k; (k/(2sqrt(N)))(X_N^2+(X_N')^2) bounds its logarithm. The resulting uniform L^2 bound makes L log L uniformly integrable. Thus this is KL convergence, not an inference from TV convergence. For Y=Z+sqrt(alpha)X, the density p_alpha satisfies partial_alpha p_alpha=-(2sqrt(alpha))^(-1) partial_y(p_alpha E[X|Y=y]), and partial_y log(p_alpha/phi)=sqrt(alpha)E[X|Y=y]. Integrating by parts yields the stated derivative, positive since Cov(X,Y)=sqrt(alpha)v. On compact positive alpha intervals Gaussian/quartic tail bounds control the derivatives; conditional Cauchy–Schwarz controls the squared conditional mean times p_alpha by the convolution with x^2 times the quartic density, giving continuity. At zero, Taylor in sqrt(alpha) uses symmetry, Gaussian L^3 control and quartic tails; the first term is alpha v(z^2-1)/2. Applying the quadratic expansion of L log L and normalization gives v^2/4. At infinity, the density of X+delta Z, 0<delta<=1, is bounded by C exp(-c|x|^4)+C Pr(|Z|>|x|/2) by splitting at |delta Z|=|x|/2. Boundedness and this tail dominate the entropy integrand, so h(X+delta Z) tends to h(X), giving the claimed log correction and constants. This is for fixed positive alpha in the finite-volume limit; the endpoint expansions apply afterward.

value.rationale: Quantifies exactly how fair-product approximation fails on the natural first nontrivial block scale in relative entropy, a strictly more tail-sensitive criterion than TV. The quartic-Gaussian profile, monotonicity and the quadratic-to-linear-with-log-correction crossover are useful benchmarks, not just a numerical sample or restatement of weak convergence.
